prompts: If all Bloops are Razzies and all Razzies are Lazzies

evaluations.response:
The two statements form a classic syllogism:

1. All Bloops are Razzies.  
2. All Razzies are Lazzies.

By the transitive property of the “all” relation, if every member of set A (Bloops) belongs to set B (Razzies), and every member of set B belongs to set C (Lazzies), then every member of set A also belongs to set C.

**Conclusion:** All Bloops are Lazzies.

This is a valid syllogism of the form **AAA‑1** (Barbara). No further conclusions about existence (e.g., “Some Lazzies are Bloops”) can be drawn unless we independently know that at least one Bloop exists.
